 India fined for Code of Conduct breach against New Zealand
 India have been penalised for breaching the ICC Code of Conduct in the fifth ODI against New Zealand.
 18 November, 2026 India have been fined 35% of their match fee for maintaining a slow over-rate in the fifth and final ODI against New Zealand , played in Mount Maunganui on 15 November.
 The visitors were found to be seven overs short of the required rate after time allowances were taken into consideration. As per Article 2.22 of the ICC Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel , the players were fined five per cent of their match fees for every over they fell short of the target (maximum cap of 50%).
 View this post on Instagram 
 India’s stand-in ODI captain Shreyas Iyer accepted the sanction imposed by Match Referee Ranjan Madugalle, so there was no need for a formal hearing.
 India signed off the series with a victory in a low-scoring final ODI. After an early wobble, the middle order came to the visitors’ rescue, with Ishan Kishan and Axar Patel scoring 46 runs apiece to guide India to 209.
 New Zealand’s response was dented by regular strikes by India, as the pacers did the bulk of the damage, bowling the Black Caps out for 187 to seal a 22-run victory and a 3-1 series win .
